author: benhur

Hi Boy

Let me try to refine your definition of a compression. Look for price movement in one direction, whereas price progress it also retrace back to consume the orders. for example, if price move upward in compression, it will constantly be eating demand leftovers.

I would re-command you break this exercise in two steps: 1. just look for the compression and mark them on the chart 2. Then learn and mark on your charts how price reacts when it visit the area of historical compression.

Try to be as precise as you can

Think of what makes a significant Supply or Demand? it is a a fresh zone - never been touched with strong away price movement.

A compression is totally the opposite scenario; The zone been pierced deep, move away is weak and slow, when you look at it visually you see no Orders.

Now, equipped with this concept, go and look for a compression - where price move slowly consuming the remaining orders.

Ifmyante wrote: Compression is one of the most important signs that price is getting ready to turn.

As price is rising into Supply, it keeps dropping as it goes, filling the buy orders left at each Demand on the way up, allowing a quick drop through the CP zone when price hits Supply.

The exact opposite is true for Compression into Demand.

Here it is explained in a video

Homework

Set up a subfolder for CP Homework and get into the charts

Find at least 20 CP setups, at HTF S/D zones, and explain what you see on each chart

Also chart the bigger picture where the CP occurred

While you're looking for CP, take the time to find at least 20 CPLQ (Liquidity) too

If you're not used to these, you can get stopped out of some fantastic trades and deeply regret not knowing why.
